author: claude-code-session-2026-08-27
choice: Raise the ANVIL steps 1-2 line-count cap from 800 to 1,000; the cap counts implementation LOC only, not test LOC
narrative: The 2,000-line total budget is unchanged and now has 1,078 lines of headroom for steps 3-9. If the total is ever at risk, the response is naming and cutting something specific, as already agreed -- not raising the total, and not trimming good code to hide under a stale sub-cap.
rationale: The 800 cap was scoped to steps 1-2 as originally defined in the directors queue, before the external (Codex) audit. Reference typing, semantic hardening, and the untracked-gate mutation harness were audit-driven additions made after that scoping and were never counted against the original number -- this is scope growth against a stale cap, not an overrun. Cutting correct, necessary code to hit a stale figure would repeat the exact failure this project already named and rejected: trimming comments to satisfy the size gate rather than splitting the file. Separately, a cap counting mutation-test code together with implementation penalizes exactly the coverage this project should not discourage -- 37 mutation cases and a scratch-git-repo test harness are a large share of the 922-line total and are precisely the code this project wants more of, not less.
reversal_cost: CHEAP -- a number in a doc/queue; reverting undoes no code, and nothing currently depends on the caps exact value.
